records.mechanism_judgment: The text says WSS operation is adjusted in response to real-time electric fluctuations and that the WSS can support the external grid, supporting both power-to-water and water-to-power directions.

evidence.quote: Fully considering the real-time electric and hydraulic fluctuation, the day-head stage optimizes the WSS to minimize the MG operational cost, and the real-time stage mitigates the MG renewable power fluctuation and respond to the EG demand. We can see the WSS can not only satisfy the MG demand, but also support the EG.

records.mechanism_judgment: The model narrative describes desalination, reservoirs, pumps, tanks, pipes, and water-use loads. The complete extracted text for this paper contains no cooling/thermoelectric-plant mention; this is a finding about the retained text, not an equation-based claim.

evidence.quote: The WSS consists of a DD, reservoirs, WPs, WTs, water pipes, and water usage loads. Living water is produced by the DD and stored in the reservoir. WPs can distribute water in the source to the hydraulic load, and WTs are used to regulate the pipe flow by storing or releasing water.

records.mechanism_judgment: The abstract says WDS pumps/tanks are operated given expected water demand and electricity prices, and that WDS energy flexibility is offered to the power-system operator, textually supporting both directions.

evidence.quote: The water distribution system operators (W-DSOs) are considered as energy-conscious entities, who run the proposed WDS operation model to optimize the operation of pumps and tanks for minimizing the operation cost of local WDSs, given the expected water demand and electricity prices of the next day. A WDS energy ﬂexibility model is proposed that is used by W-DSOs in order to calculate and offer the feasible ﬂexible energy capacity to the power system operator.

evidence.quote: The relevant simulation data exchanged between the power system and wa-ter network simulations included EPS network conﬁgurations, pump electric power consumption as an identiﬁable component of power system loads, and thermal generation cooling water requirements, which were used as node demands within the water system.
